content: 1. The Xpert MTB/RIF assay is recommended as the initial diagnostic test for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) specimens in patients suspected of having tuberculosis (TB) meningitis. This recommendation is based on the urgency for rapid diagnosis, despite the very low quality of evidence. 2. In adults and children with signs and symptoms of extrapulmonary TB, Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert Ultra are recommended as initial diagnostic tests for TB meningitis using CSF specimens. The evidence for test accuracy is of moderate certainty for Xpert MTB/RIF and low certainty for Xpert Ultra. 3. For extrapulmonary TB, Xpert MTB/RIF may be used as the initial diagnostic test in specimens such as lymph node aspirates, lymph node biopsies, pleural fluid, peritoneal fluid, pericardial fluid, synovial fluid, or urine. The certainty of evidence varies: moderate for pleural fluid, low for lymph node aspirates, peritoneal fluid, synovial fluid, and urine, and very low for pericardial fluid and lymph node biopsies. 4. Xpert Ultra may be used as the initial diagnostic test for extrapulmonary TB in lymph node aspirates and lymph node biopsies. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence. 5. Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra should be used for detecting rifampicin resistance in adults and children with extrapulmonary TB, rather than culture and drug susceptibility testing (DST). The evidence for test accuracy is of high certainty for Xpert MTB/RIF and low certainty for Xpert Ultra. 6. Xpert MTB/RIF is recommended for diagnosing disseminated TB using blood specimens. 7. In adults with pulmonary TB symptoms and an Xpert Ultra trace-positive result on the initial test, repeated testing with Ultra is not recommended. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 8. In children with pulmonary TB symptoms in settings with a pretest probability below 5% and a negative Xpert MTB/RIF result on the initial test, repeated testing with Xpert MTB/RIF in sputum, gastric fluid, nasopharyngeal aspirate, or stool specimens is not recommended. The certainty of evidence is low for sputum and very low for other specimen types. 9. In children with pulmonary TB symptoms in settings with a pretest probability of 5% or more and a negative Xpert MTB/RIF result on the initial test, repeated testing with Xpert MTB/RIF (for a total of two tests) in sputum, gastric fluid, nasopharyngeal aspirate, or stool specimens may be used. This is a conditional recommendation with low certainty of evidence for sputum and very low for other specimen types. 10. In children with pulmonary TB symptoms in settings with a pretest probability below 5% and a negative Xpert Ultra result on the initial test, repeated testing with Xpert Ultra in sputum or nasopharyngeal aspirate specimens is not recommended. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence. 11. The TrueNat MTB and MTB Plus assays, developed in India, may be used as initial diagnostic tests for pulmonary TB in adults and children, replacing smear microscopy or culture. This is a conditional recommendation with moderate certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 12. For patients with a positive TrueNat MTB or MTB Plus result, the TrueNat MTB-RIF Dx assay may be used as an initial test for rifampicin resistance, replacing culture and phenotypic DST. This is a conditional recommendation with very low certainty of evidence for test accuracy. 13. The TrueNat system uses real-time micro-PCR technology to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance in DNA extracted from sputum specimens. It is designed for use in peripheral laboratories with minimal infrastructure and can provide results in under one hour. 14. The diagnostic performance of TrueNat assays has been evaluated in microscopy centers in India, but further assessment of operational characteristics and acceptability in intended settings is needed to confirm assay performance. 15. The WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis recommend the use of molecular assays, including Xpert MTB/RIF, Xpert Ultra, and TrueNat, for the rapid diagnosis of TB and rifampicin resistance in adults and children. These guidelines emphasize the importance of evidence-based recommendations to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes.
